articles.title: A.J. Brown says he's not 100 percent after returning from high-ankle sprain: 'I'm pushing through'
articles.summary: A.J. Brown missed multiple games this season due to a high-ankle sprain.
articles.body:
New England Patriots wideout A.J. Brown was supposed to be the key to unlocking an even stronger offense in 2026. While an early injury scuttled those plans, Brown was able to return to action in Week 6. So far, though, he hasn't looked like himself.

In two games since he's been back, Brown has been targeted 16 times, but has hauled in just six of those balls for 75 yards. He's also fumbled once since his return. That production is far below what the Patriots expected when the team gave up a first-round pick for the wideout.

Turns out, there's a reason for that. Though Brown is back, he's still battling through the after effects of his high-ankle sprain. The 29-year-old admitted as much Wednesday, telling Boston Sports Journal he's " pushing through " it right now.

When asked whether he was still trying to regain his explosiveness after the injury, Brown said:

"Yeah, sometimes, you know, I see it, and sometimes, I'm pushing through," he admitted. "But none of that stuff even matters. I'm out here, so I'm going."

Despite that, the Patriots haven't limited Brown's playing time since he's been back. The wideout played 76 percent of the team's offensive snaps in Week 6 and 91 percent of the team's offensive snaps in Week 7.

Injuries have certainly played a role in that decision, as the team is without Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins at the moment.

Those injuries make it hard to project when Brown will feel completely back to normal. The Patriots do have a bye in Week 11, giving Brown at least another week in the season to rest the injury, though it's unclear if that will be enough.

When healthy, Brown has proven to be one of the best receivers in the game. Despite missing a few games in both 2024 and 2025, he still managed to exceed 1,000 receiving yards in each season.

That streak could be put to the test in 2026, though. In the three games he's played, Brown has just 101 total yards. He would need some massive performances moving forward to get to 1,000 yards on the season, a much tougher task if Brown is still dealing with his high-ankle sprain.

Ultimately, the Patriots don't necessarily need that level of performance out of Brown during the regular season. If the star receiver is fully healthy for the playoffs, that's all that matters as they look to bounce back after last season's Super Bowl loss.

articles.title: Did Bears overpay for Jeffery Simmons? What recent DL trades from Cowboys, Rams, Packers might teach
articles.summary: Initial reaction from NFL executives, talent evaluators and coaches questioned the price the Bears paid to poach Simmons, even if his talents are undeniable.
articles.body:
In the short term, the Minnesota Vikings, Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions should shudder.

Kyler Murray, Jordan Love and Jared Goff's lives just got harder.

Offensive success against the Chicago Bears won't come as easily after Thursday morning. Good luck to the NFC North quarterbacks.

The Chicago Bears and Tennessee Titans agreed to a trade for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons , according to multiple reports. The Bears sent their 2027 first-round pick, 2028 first-round pick and 2027 fourth-round pick to Tennessee in exchange for Simmons and the Titans' 2028 fifth, per the Titans.

Simmons immediately upgrades a managing-but-inefficient defense. Through seven games in Tennessee this year, he registered four sacks, a forced fumble and fumble recovery, 13 pressures, nine quarterback hits and 38 tackles. No defensive tackle has won his pass-rush reps more than Simmons' 27% clip, per ESPN's pass-rush win rate metric . Simmons was that efficient even as he played high-volume snaps, pass-rushing 124 times in seven games while facing double teams on 84% of snaps, per ESPN.

The Bears' top player on that list before Thursday was Grady Jarrett, who ranked 18th with a 16% win rate.

So no one's doubting that the Bears are better now, better this season and better in 2027 as they acquire Simmons. But initial reaction from executives, talent evaluators and coaches across the league questioned the price the Bears paid to poach Simmons .

"Great trade value-wise [for Tennessee] long term," one AFC assistant coach told Yahoo Sports.

An NFC executive deemed the price "a lot" when an executive from a second AFC team said they congratulated Titans counterparts on the return.

What would executives and talent evaluators from other teams pay for Simmons?

One NFC executive valued Simmons as worth a first- and a second-round pick. An AFC executive said Simmons is indeed "very, very good" and thus would warrant "maybe a one and change." An executive from another NFC team noted value differs based on a team's current needs at the position, but for the Bears, they'd consider a 2027 first and 2028 third worth acquiring him. (Teams differ on whether they view the value of picks consistent across years or whether they discount the value of a later-year pick due to the limited ability to gain value from the asset in the interim.)

So will trading two firsts and change prove worthwhile for the Bears? A look at recent blockbuster defensive line trades call that into question.

How Micah Parsons, Myles Garrett, Quinnen Williams have impacted their teams so far

There is always the risk of injury for any player acquisition. Teams calculate cost-benefit analyses by the player, often considering past injuries and age as the top predictor of future injuries.

So the Green Bay Packers' 2025 trade for Micah Parsons and the Los Angeles Rams' 2026 trade for Myles Garrett are so far more unlucky than they were reckless. But each can serve as a cautionary tale.

The Packers sent their 2026 first-round pick, 2027 first-round pick and defensive tackle Kenny Clark to the Dallas Cowboys in August 2025 in exchange for Parsons, who had earned four Pro Bowl berths and two first-team All-Pro nods in his four Dallas years. Parsons was productive in 14 games last season, collecting 12.5 sacks, 41 tackles and two forced fumbles. Then he tore his ACL on Dec. 14. He has yet to return to practice.

The Rams sent a 2027 first-round pick, 2028 second-round pick, 2029 third-round pick and edge rusher Jared Verse to the Cleveland Browns on June 1 in exchange for Garrett, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year.

Garrett played 40 snaps in LA's season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers but clearly was not himself. The Rams explained later that swelling in Garrett's knee was too intense to play through productively, and he would require surgery. Seven weeks later, Garrett has yet to return to practice .

Does that mean each trade is destined to be a bust? No. But the losses incurred while Parsons and Garrett have been sidelined impact not only the value of the payday their teams are contributing but also the value of the draft picks sent away. The Rams expected their 2027 first-round pick would be in the late 20s at the highest and hoped it was pick No. 32. They surprised the league by selecting quarterback Ty Simpson in the 2026 first round in part because they didn't anticipate a 2027 first being within range of a quarterback. Eleven weeks remain in the regular season. But the Rams currently sit at 3-4, which means the Browns are projected for the 14th overall pick, per Tankathon.com . At 4-3, the Packers' 2027 first currently pegs the Cowboys to select 20th.

"It's hard to bank that far out in advance," an NFC executive said of teams hoping their traded-away firsts will arrive late in the round.

The Cowboys' trade-deadline acquisition of Quinnen Williams a year ago in some ways has proven even less successful. Williams has provided defensive leadership and stayed healthy. But the Cowboys' defense has struggled even with him on the field.

Sure, they're better with him: Since the beginning of 2025, the Cowboys' defense has allowed 356.9 total yards per game with Williams compared to 402.9 without him, per TruMedia Sports. He's helped them down from 143.9 to 122.5 rushing yards per game, 259 to 234.4 passing yards (he has not been the only variable during the that period). But even at 376 yards per game, the Cowboys rank second-worst in the league in yards allowed across 2025-2026, and they're third worst this year alone. The Cowboys have allowed more points this season than all but the New Orleans Saints, Las Vegas Raiders and Arizona Cardinals — rebuilding teams. Across the two seasons, only the Cardinals are leakier.

Will Simmons buck the recent trends and meaningfully improve the Bears?

"He's a really good player," an NFC executive said. "Definitely makes them better immediately."

Why elite DTs like Simmons 'disarm' offenses in a way edge rushers don't

The reality: If the Bears win the Super Bowl, advance to the Super Bowl or perhaps even advance to a conference championship with a heavily contributing Simmons, no one will care about the future picks that may or may not have panned out.

Another reality: Even when considering the recent heavy-hitting defensive line trades, this move remains unprecedented. Simmons is the first defensive tackle in the common draft era (since 1967) to be traded for multiple first-round picks, per ESPN Research .

If healthy, he can help the 5-2 Bears catch 6-0 Minnesota. He can help a defense that has benefited greatly from staying off the field (the Bears lead the league with a 35:30 average time of possession) while struggling on a per-play basis. Chicago ranks eighth in yards allowed per game (313.4) but last in yards allowed per play (6.25). No team has allowed more pass yards per play than the Bears defense's 8.15.

Edge rushers remain a vaunted bunch in the NFL. But elite pass-rushing defensive tackles are frustrating offensive coordinators and quarterbacks at rising rates.

"It's not like he's the right defensive end that you can choose to run away from or always help to — it's really hard to build help elements into a game plan for a nose tackle," Bengals offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher told Yahoo Sports during training camp. "It's just not something you're used to doing and your flexibility and how you do it is not nearly as great as when you start talking about trying to help edge players and guys of that nature. There's only so much you can do."

Acquiring and developing interior offensive linemen, as the Seattle Seahawks (ironically the Bears' next opponent) just did with Quenton Nelson , helps. But without the top-shelf talent, offenses struggle against teams with top defensive tackles.

"It just disarms you because I don't know what you do to counteract that other than you just really focus on the technique of this interior line and you've got to be really cognizant of what types of schemes you're trying to run and how often that guy's truly one-on-one," Pitcher said.

"So if he's able to create pocket push or penetration, it's right there in your lap. And when an end creates penetration, hopefully you're firm enough inside that you can step up and climb escape lanes. When that [defensive tackle] is in your face, your escape lanes are out. That's never a good thing. Running sideways and backwards at quarterback in the NFL is a good way to not play very long.

Consider that, and one NFC talent evaluator deeming Simmons "MUCH better" than Williams — "not even in the same category" — and the Bears' price suddenly looks less wild if still steep.

The ceiling for Chicago's newest acquisition is high. How close will Simmons come to reaching it?

articles.title: ‘No Shame, No Guilt,’ ‘He’s Disgusting’ — NFL Fans Rip Packers RB Josh Jacobs for Apparent Handcuffs Celebration After TD vs. Panthers
articles.summary: Josh Jacobs returned to the Green Bay Packers in Week 7 after missing the first six games of the 2026 season while on the NFL’s Commissioner’s Exempt List fo...
articles.body:
Josh Jacobs returned to the Green Bay Packers in Week 7 after missing the first six games of the 2026 season while on the NFL's Commissioner's Exempt List following his May arrest in a domestic dispute. But two weeks into his return, fans were aghast at one particular display from the three-time Pro Bowler.

After scoring a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers on Thursday Night Football, Jacobs did a celebration in the end zone that seemed to look like him walking with handcuffs, with his hands tied behind his back. Given the severity of the lawsuit, fans were infuriated by his gesture.

A domestic dispute in May 2026 led to his arrest. Initially facing five counts of battery, criminal damage to property, disorderly conduct, strangulation and suffocation, as well as intimidation of a victim, he was formally charged with battery and criminal damage to property.

Pleading no contest to both charges, he was placed on one year of supervision, alongside restitution, a fine, and a no-contact order. It also led to him missing the first six games of the season, before returning in Week 7.

But in Week 8, things took an ugly turn. After scoring a second-quarter touchdown, Jacobs performed a celebration that some social media users interpreted as mimicking someone being handcuffed. The gesture immediately drew criticism given his recent legal case.

Speaking after the game, the Packers star alleged that the broadcast did not show the full celebration. "It was more to it than that," Jacobs said. "They stopped showing the celebration after that. Like I said, it is what it is." Jacobs added that he was instead modeling his celebration after a gospel song called "Break Every Chain."

"The guys did it with me," Jacobs said. "I didn't think it was going to be something that could be perceived a certain type of way. But it's 2026, and it is what it is."

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

The official account of the "Pardon My Take" podcast wondered , "Did Josh Jacobs just hit a Handcuff Celebration?"

One fan was shocked at the way the NFL was handling the situation, writing, "Yes, remember when players used to get punished for committing crimes like Ray Rice."

Another believed it was a problem unique to sports and just one other role, as he argued, "He's disgusting. I hate that professional sports is the one profession where this type of behaviour doesn't end in termination."

For one fan, it was a clear double standard from the NFL, as he claimed, "The NFL will allow Josh Jacobs to play and then try to lecture the public about social issues."

Another fan didn't mince words as he exclaimed, "Embarrassing that you're allowing him to play," tagging both the NFL and the NFL Commissioner's account.

As one fan rhetorically asked , "Is Josh Jacobs not the most disgusting human right now?" another fan mocked , "He'll probably sue to keep this video hidden, too."

It remains to be seen if the league takes further action against Jacobs for his display. But given the sensitivity around the issue, there will be more than a few calls from fans for the league to look into the matter.

articles.title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ kids steal the Halloween spotlight with pumpkin heads in adorable family snap
articles.summary: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes took their three kids to a pumpkin patch this week, and Brittany shared the day on Instagram Stories on Wednesday, Oct. 28.
articles.body: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes took their three kids to a pumpkin patch this week, and Brittany shared the day on Instagram Stories on Wednesday, Oct. 28. Sterling, 5, Bronze, 3, and Golden, 21 months, posed on hay bales and sat on carousel animals with their dad. Not every photo came out sharp, and Brittany said so herself. The outing follows an Oct. 14 press conference where the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback admitted he had forgotten Halloween until his wife asked about costumes. Patrick and Brittany are both 31, and the season is in full swing.Mahomes family spends Wednesday at the pumpkin patchBrittany, a former soccer player, posted several Stories from the outing. The first was a slightly blurry shot of the kids on a haystack among pumpkins. She wrote over it, “Out with the clear pictures,” and added a crying laughing emoji. Anyone who has tried to photograph three young children at once will understand.The other pictures were sharper. Sterling grinned from a flamingo on a carousel. Patrick stood between Bronze and Golden, who smiled from their own animals on the ride. A final shot showed Sterling posing on top of bear statues, with lights glowing in the trees behind her.Patrick forgot about Halloween until Brittany askedPatrick had other things on his mind when Halloween came up on Oct. 14. Season routines had pushed the holiday out of his head, he told reporters at a press conference.“Once you get in season, you’re focused on that week. You focus on that week, then you try to win that week and then you move on to the next week,” the Chiefs athlete said. “It surprised me. I forgot about Halloween.”Brittany was the one who brought it up. “Brittany asked me, ‘What are we going to be for Halloween?’ I’m like, ‘I didn’t even think about that,’ ” he admitted.A reporter asked what the family would wear. “I can’t tell now,” Patrick replied. “There’s options because you never know with kids. So we have multiple options. I don’t even know yet. I still have a couple of options.”Brittany keeps sharing the fall seasonBrittany has been posting fall content for weeks. On Oct. 3, she shared photos from Johnson Farms Plants and Pumpkins with the caption “It’s fall yall🍂” The kids met animals, picked apples and did arts and crafts. Other pictures showed the family together and posing with mascots.Football has been part of the routine too. She posted shots of herself and the kids cheering on Patrick at a Chiefs game, captioned “The best times🥹❤️,” on Oct. 21. Back on Aug. 4, the family watched training camp at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, Mo., as Patrick reported for his 10th NFL season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: A Tom Brady romance, a ‘Backstabber’ accusation and 15 years of friendship: Inside the supermodel fallout
articles.summary: Tom Brady’s reported romance with Victoria’s Secret model Candice Swanepoel has sparked speculation about a bitter split between Swanepoel and her
articles.body: Tom Brady’s reported romance with Victoria’s Secret model Candice Swanepoel has sparked speculation about a bitter split between Swanepoel and her longtime friend Joan Smalls. According to reports, Smalls and Brady were romantically involved on and off for about a year, making the latest relationship rumors especially sensitive given the models’ 15-year friendship. Alleged social media comments accusing an unnamed person of betrayal have added to the attention, though neither model has publicly confirmed the full story. For now, the reported fallout remains a mix of insider claims, cryptic posts and unanswered questions.Joan Smalls’ ‘Backstabber’ comments put her friendship with Candice Swanepoel under scrutinyThe reported rift became a talking point after Smalls allegedly responded to a fan asking about her friendship with Swanepoel. In comments that were later deleted, she reportedly wrote, “I'm not friends with backstabbers.” Another message appeared to explain her frustration, referring to broken trust and a lack of respect after years of friendship."And the disrespect and carelessness in how they treat you is so unimaginable. There’s no going back. Some people lack humility and moral compass," she reportedly wrote."And the way they gaslight, lie and minimize your feelings is the worst slap in the face after 15yrs of friendship. Not a sorry said or written. Onwards and upwards!!!"The timing fueled speculation. Both models attended the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show, but fans noticed they were not seen together as they had been in the past. Reports also linked their apparent distance to Brady, with sources claiming Smalls felt blindsided by her friend's reported relationship with the retired quarterback.Still, the distinction between reported claims and confirmed facts matters. Neither model has publicly laid out the full reason for the apparent tension, and Brady has not confirmed a relationship with Swanepoel. The online comments may offer clues about hurt feelings, but they do not establish exactly what happened between the longtime friends.Candice Swanepoel’s response leaves the door open on a 15-year friendshipSwanepoel's representative offered a measured response when asked about the reports, stressing the model's preference for privacy rather than addressing the alleged romantic dispute directly."Candice has always been exceptionally private about her personal life, with her focus remaining on raising her children. She and Joan share a longstanding history and a friendship that Candice will always respect."That statement neither confirms a feud nor dismisses the history between the two models. Their friendship stretches back roughly 15 years, through careers that have often placed them in the same fashion circles and major industry events. A dispute involving a reported romance would therefore carry a different weight from an ordinary celebrity dating rumor.Brady, meanwhile, has been linked to several women since finalizing his divorce from Gisele Bündchen in October 2022. His reported connection with Swanepoel has now brought attention to a personal situation involving two established figures in the modeling world.For now, the biggest unanswered question is not whether Brady and Swanepoel are dating, but whether a friendship that lasted 15 years can withstand the reported breach of trust. Until the people involved speak more clearly, the claims should remain just that: reports, not a settled account of what ended the relationship between two longtime friends.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "Long standing beef": Patrick Mahomes sends clear message after Chiefs bring in Justin Tucker
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes is keeping his focus on football as the Kansas City Chiefs welcome a familiar rival into their building.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes is keeping his focus on football as the Kansas City Chiefs welcome a familiar rival into their building. Justin Tucker's arrival has raised eyebrows, not only because of Harrison Butker's recent struggles but also because of his past confrontation with Mahomes and Travis Kelce. However, the Chiefs quarterback has made one thing clear: there is no lingering tension between them. With Kansas City preparing for a crucial AFC West clash against Denver, Tucker's signing could have a much bigger impact than expected.Patrick Mahomes addresses past tension with Justin TuckerTucker's arrival in Kansas City brings back memories of an awkward moment before the 2023 AFC Championship Game. The Baltimore Ravens kicker had placed his equipment in an area where Mahomes and other Chiefs players were warming up.The situation quickly turned into a heated exchange. Kelce threw away Tucker's kicking tee and footballs, while Mahomes also became involved. The incident attracted plenty of attention, with questions about whether the players had developed a personal rivalry.However, Mahomes has dismissed suggestions of any lasting disagreement. Speaking to reporters on October 28, he explained that the incident was simply part of the competitive atmosphere surrounding such an important game.“I mean, the relationships, we haven’t had a lot of conversations ’cause he was obviously on the Ravens and I was on the Chiefs. But it wasn’t like we ever had any long standing beef or anything like that,” Mahomes said. “I think at that moment, it was just competitors being competitors. And it was a big moment for everybody’s career, and you’re playing the AFC Championship Game.“And he’s been a big-time kicker for a long time. And me and Trav were obviously competing and we wanted to go out there and win. And that stuff happened, but then you move on from that. I mean, at the end of the day, we’re just playing a game.”His comments suggest that the old disagreement will not affect Tucker's attempt to settle into his new team.Justin Tucker signing puts Harrison Butker under pressureThe Chiefs signed Tucker to their practice squad on Wednesday after holding tryouts with three kickers. He impressed the coaching staff by converting all 30 attempts during the session, beating Harrison Mevis and Ben Sauls for the opportunity.Kansas City has a clear reason to explore another option. Butker has converted just 11 of 16 field-goal attempts through six games this season. His two misses against the Seattle Seahawks on October 25 proved particularly costly in the Chiefs' 20-3 defeat.Head coach Andy Reid has acknowledged the problem and expects Butker to respond.“He understands the business and how it works. We had a practice squad position open. For security, we brought (Tucker) in and put him in that spot that we had open. Butker gets it. He knows that’s part of the business. He’s struggled a little bit. He gets it, he needs to pick it up a little bit.”Tucker brings an impressive career record, including seven Pro Bowl selections and the second-highest field-goal percentage in NFL history. He also has experience performing under pressure, including his famous 47-yard overtime winner against Denver in the 2012 playoffs.For now, Butker remains Kansas City's kicker heading into Week 8. However, Tucker's arrival has created genuine competition. If Butker cannot rediscover his accuracy, the Chiefs may have little reason to keep waiting.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Packers' Josh Jacobs insists he wasn't making light of his arrest during TD celebration
articles.summary: Jacobs scored twice in his second game since returning to the Packers, but had a controversial celebration after one of them.
articles.body:
In just his second game back on the field with the Packers since being on the NFL's commissioner exempt list, Josh Jacobs helped power his team to a 27-19 win on Thursday night.

Jacobs finished with just 39 rushing yards, but added six catches and a pair of touchdowns in Green Bay's victory over Carolina. The running back's celebration after one of those scores, however, became controversial.

Jacobs, who was arrested earlier this year and charged with misdemeanor battery and destruction of property, appeared to put his hands behind his back as a touchdown celebration, but provided another explanation for his actions postgame.

Here's what Jacobs said about his touchdown celebration against the Panthers .

Josh Jacobs explains TD celebration vs. Panthers

After Jacobs scored his first touchdown of the night in the second quarter, he put his hands behind his back, leading fans to question whether he was making light of his arrest earlier in 2026.

In May, Jacobs was arrested in Wisconsin following an incident with a woman at his home. He was booked on five domestic battery-related charges, later charged with misdemeanor battery and destruction of property.

That incident led to Jacobs being placed on the commissioner's exempt list to start the 2026 season, missing six games before he was allowed to re-join the Packers las week. He remains subject to a potential NFL suspension for the league's personal conduct policy.

Fans criticized Jacobs for appearing to make light of his arrest, but the running back provided another explanation for his celebration against the Panthers, saying it was an ode to a gospel song called "Break Every Chain." He said that the broadcast didn't capture the full celebration.

"They didn't even get the whole celebration," Jacobs said."It was f---ing one second that they just showed me."

Jacobs also said that he and teammate Savion Williams came up with two celebrations for his return.

"Basically, last week, we said the first celebration, when I score, I was going to thank God -- that's what I did last week," Jacobs said. "The second one was going to be 'Break Every Chain.' It's a gospel song. That was going to be the next celebration. It's just a correlation, but like I said, the media [is] going to run with it. They're going to make it something that it wasn't, but it is what it is."

The running back added that other Packers teammates did the same celebration.

"I didn't think it was going to be a thing that can be perceived a certain type of way," Jacobs said, per ESPN . "But it's 2026, and it is what it is."

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb said something wild about the Arizona Cardinals
articles.summary: CeeDee Lamb has never beaten the Cardinals since he was drafted by the Cowboys.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals will face the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday in Week 8. The Cardinals are struggling this season, sitting at 2-5. But the Cowboys are 3-4 and have not beaten the Cardinals since 2017.

It has gotten the attention of receiver CeeDee Lamb, one of the best pass-catchers in the NFL.

Since he entered the league in 2020, he and the Cowboys have lost four times to the Cardinals, which led Lamb to say this about the matchup.

"Yeah, it's just crazy," Lamb said via Dallas' team site . "[We were] being very, very relaxed, and they punched us in the mouth every single time. They've always had more energy. They were more excited, regardless of if it was a 12 o'clock, Sunday night or Monday night.

"We've played them in prime time. They beat us there, so we need to treat them as if they are a Super Bowl-contending team, which they may be, you know what I'm saying? Hats off to them in their prep, and we've just got to go match them, if not overpower that."

The Cardinals certainly are not a Super Bowl-contending team. They have looked mostly like one of the worst teams in the NFL this season. However, they seem to find ways to win against the Cowboys.

The Cardinals have never lost at AT&T Stadium, which opened in 2009.

The Cowboys are seven-point home favorites in this game. The Cowboys and Cardinals kick off at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday (11 a.m. Arizona time).

Get more Cardinals and NFL coverage from Cards Wire's Jess Root and others by listening to the latest on the Rise Up, See Red podcast. Subscribe on Spotify , YouTube or Apple Podcasts .

articles.title: Josh Allen vs Lamar Jackson: Two MVP careers, different playoff stories and one question about who will define the AFC era
articles.summary: Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson meet Sunday at Highmark Stadium, and Jackson's ankle decides how much the game means.
articles.body: Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson meet Sunday at Highmark Stadium, and Jackson's ankle decides how much the game means. The Ravens quarterback has not played since Week 4 and missed three straight games. Coach Jesse Minter has sounded encouraging, though his status stayed unsettled this week. Buffalo is 5-1, Baltimore 4-3. Jackson has two MVP awards, Allen one, and neither has won a Super Bowl. Allen holds the playoff edge between them, winning both postseason meetings, in January 2021 and January 2025, but his exit in Denver last season showed that edge guarantees nothing in the AFC race.Josh Allen vs Lamar Jackson: Two MVP careers, two different playoff storiesJackson won MVP unanimously in 2019 and again in 2023. Allen took the award in 2024, and the vote was one of the closest in recent years. The stats show why. Jackson threw for 4,172 yards and 41 touchdowns with four interceptions that season, and ran for 915 yards. Allen threw for 3,731 yards and 28 touchdowns, but he also ran for 531 yards and 12 scores, and Buffalo finished 13-4 to Baltimore's 12-5.The playoffs split them. Jackson is 3-5 in the postseason. Their first meeting, a 17-3 Bills win, ended early for him because of a concussion. The second came in Buffalo in January 2025, when he threw an interception and lost a fumble in the first half. Allen scored twice on the ground, the Bills forced three turnovers, and Mark Andrews dropped a two-point try with 1:33 left in a 27-25 Buffalo win. Baltimore missed the playoffs the following season, so that night still closes out his résumé.Allen's story is messier, and last season made it worse. The AFC field had no Patrick Mahomes, Jackson or Joe Burrow, and Allen's team could not take advantage of that. Buffalo beat Jacksonville in the wild-card round, then lost 33-30 in overtime at Denver. Allen turned the ball over four times, after going 427 postseason snaps without a fumble or interception. "Feel like I let my teammates down tonight," he said afterward. He is also 0-7 in overtime games for his career.The two problems look different. Jackson's is a pattern across eight games. Allen's is a short list of bad endings, set against efficiency numbers that once ranked first among playoff quarterbacks since 2020. Allen has reached two AFC title games and Jackson one. Both lost to Kansas City.Sunday gives the AFC race an early testAcross seven meetings, Jackson has won three of five regular-season games, and Allen has won both playoff games. Oddsmakers still have the Bills favored on Sunday, even with Jackson possibly back. Baltimore lost its second straight game without him last weekend, and the Ravens average 395 yards in his starts this season.Minter is the Ravens' new head coach, and receiver Zay Flowers said in May that people would see a refreshed Jackson. The ankle has interrupted that plan. Jackson's 2025 was already injury-affected, so his health is a theme as much as his playoff record.Allen opened the year with 269 passing yards, 65 rushing yards and four total touchdowns in Week 1, and he leads the early MVP odds. He finished third in the vote last season, with two first-place votes. Matthew Stafford won it by one first-place vote over Drake Maye. Allen is also the first player in NFL history with five straight 40-touchdown seasons, counting passing and rushing.Sunday is not January. Still, Allen has beaten Jackson both times it counted most.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Patriots vs. Dolphins weather forecast for NFL Week 8
articles.summary: Up-to-date weather forecast for Sunday’s game between the Patriots and Dolphins.
articles.body:
The last time the New England Patriots traveled to Florida, they were soundly beaten 35-6 by the Jacksonville Jaguars. One of the contributing factors to that loss appeared to be the team struggling with the heat and humidity.

At least one of the two might not have that big an impact come Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins. According to NFL Weather , temperatures at Hard Rock Stadium will not exceed 78°F during the Week 8 contest between the two division rivals. The National Weather Service , meanwhile, projects highs near 82°F for the day.

What will differentiate that game from the Jaguars one, however, is the precipitation. Whereas that Week 3 contest was played in sunny conditions, this one won't: the chance of rain has been calculated at 80% with showers and thunderstorms an option.

In addition, wind gusts of up to 26 mph are projected for the area (although in-stadium conditions may vary).

All in all, however, the weather could have an impact on the contest — as could the Patriots' conditioning.

"We have to be conditioned," said head coach Mike Vrabel this week. "The better that we play, the more we possess the ball, the fresher we'll stay defensively. Hopefully we get the receivers into a rotation. The backs, we rotate. I don't think that the offensive linemen will necessarily rotate. We may play a couple guys based on who's available. That remains to be seen. The edge guys, we rotate. We try to rotate along the defensive line. We like to have our best players available to help us win."

Kickoff between the Patriots and Dolphins on Sunday is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Jets, Titans, Browns will control the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft
articles.summary: The Jets, Browns, and Titans have made significant trades to boost their draft assets. We show how they control the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season has yet to hit the midway point.

But some teams — and their fans — are already thinking about the 2027 NFL Draft.

There is a long way to go until the league descends upon the nation's capital for the annual player entry draft, and many — many — mock drafts to come until then. And while the final order for the 2027 NFL Draft is far from finalized, some teams are already sitting in a very good position due to previous trades.

In fact three teams (the New York Jets, the Cleveland Browns, and the Tennessee Titans) already have multiple picks in the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft.

Will more teams join them as we approach the annual trade deadline?

Here is how the first round currently stands, as well as a look at the teams with multiple first-round picks, and how they got there.

Here is how the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft currently stands, bearing in mind there is a long way to go until this order is finalized:

Again, this is before all the games in Week 7 are played, so there is a long way to go until this order is finalized.

But if the draft were held today, the Chargers would have the first pick.

And the Jets would have three in the top 12.

Why the Jets, Browns, and Titans could control the 2027 NFL Draft

Ahead of the NFL's 2026 trade deadline three teams — the Jets, Browns, and Titans — have multiple first-round picks.

At the moment the Browns have a pair of picks in the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft. One is their own, which with Cleveland entering Week 7 with a 5-2 record, slots in at No. 26 for the moment.

The other comes from the Los Angeles Rams, courtesy of this summer's Myles Garrett trade. In that deal the Browns traded Garrett to the Rams in exchange for Jared Verse, a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second-round pick, and a 2029 conditional round pick (either a third-round pick, or a first-round pick if the Rams were to trade Garrett to a team in the AFC North).

With the Rams entering Week 7 with a 3-4 record, that pick slots in at No. 14 for the moment.

Like the Browns, the Titans currently hold a pair of picks in the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft. one is their own, which would be No. 2 as the Titans etner Week 7 with a 1-6 record.

The other? That comes from the Chicago Bears, thanks to Thursday's trade involving defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons. In that deal the Bears acquired Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick in exchange for a 2027 first-round pick, a 2027 fourth-round pick, and a 2028 first-round pick.

With Chicago currently 5-2, the Bears' pick is at No. 28 at the moment.

Then we get to the Jets, who currently hold three first-round picks in the 2027 NFL Draft.

One is their own, which slots in at No. 11 for the moment thanks to New York's 2-5 record.

But their first, at least right now, would be at No. 7, thanks to the Indianapolis Colts. Last season the Jets traded cornerback Sauce Gardner to Indianapolis for wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, a 2026 first-round pick (which the Jets used at No. 16 to draft tight end Kenyon Sadiq), and a 2027 first-round pick.

Then their third pick comes, at least for the moment, from the Dallas Cowboys.

The Jets also traded defensive tackle Quinnen Williams to Dallas in exchange for defensive lineman Mazi Smith, a 2026 second-round pick (which the Jets then traded to the Detroit Lions in exchange for picks at No. 50 and No. 128 last year), and a 2027 first-round pick.

But that trade happened in November, after the preseason trade involving Micah Parsons. In August of 2025, the Cowboys sent Parsons to the Packers in exchange for Kenny Clark, a 2026 first-round pick (which Dallas traded to the Philadelphia Eagles), and a 2027 first-round pick.

Returning to the trade between the Jets and the Cowboys, the Jets will receive either the Cowboys' own first-round pick, or the pick Dallas received from Green Bay, whichever one is better.

At the moment, the Cowboys are 3-4, and after Thursday night's win over the Carolina Panthers, the Packers are 5-3. So if the 2027 NFL Draft were to happen today, the Jets' third pick would be the Cowboys' own selection at No. 12, and Dallas would be on the clock with Green Bay's pick at No. 20.

articles.title: Packers' Xavier McKinney says NFL fined him 'a lot' for  criticizing refs after loss to Lions
articles.summary: McKinney said the fine was at least $25,000, the minimum amount for criticizing officials.
articles.body:
Xavier McKinney said he was fined "a lot" of money by the NFL for ripping officials during his postgame comments following last Sunday's loss to the Detroit Lions .

The Green Bay Packers safety, speaking after Thursday's 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers , would not divulge the exact amount, but the minimum fine for criticizing officiating is $25,000, as Puka Nacua found out last season . McKinney told reporters the total was at least that amount.

During the Lions game, Packers head coach Matt LaFleur got into numerous animated discussions with officials and said afterward there were "some tough calls." Those calls were a pair of roughing the passer penalties and an unnecessary roughness call.

LaFleur wasn't willing to pin the game on what he believed were bad calls. McKinney, on the other hand, didn't hold back, saying calls are "kind of f***ing up" games.

Understanding that his comments might draw a punishment from the NFL, McKinney didn't shy away from his criticism.

"I don't know how the NFL's going to treat it, but I'm not a big fan of the refs right now," McKinney said on Sunday. "I don't think it's great officiating, if I'm being completely honest. I think it's bulls*** a lot of the times." … "It's annoying even talking about it because these are critical drives throughout the game, and we might have a drive where we're getting stops but you're calling penalties and it's like, this is not a penalty," McKinney said. "To me, it just don't really make any sense, and it's killing our momentum, it's killing our drives, and it's kind of f***ing up the games, if I'm being honest."

"I don't know how the NFL's going to treat it, but I'm not a big fan of the refs right now," McKinney said on Sunday. "I don't think it's great officiating, if I'm being completely honest. I think it's bulls*** a lot of the times."

"It's annoying even talking about it because these are critical drives throughout the game, and we might have a drive where we're getting stops but you're calling penalties and it's like, this is not a penalty," McKinney said. "To me, it just don't really make any sense, and it's killing our momentum, it's killing our drives, and it's kind of f***ing up the games, if I'm being honest."

McKinney said he was fine with the league taking money out of his pocket because he felt his comments could help his team in the future.

The NFL reacted in another way to the officiating in that Packers-Lions game. According to Football Zebras , the officiating crew, led by Alex Moore, has been moved off of Sunday night's Philadelphia Eagles-Washington Commanders game and will now work the New England Patriots-Miami Dolphins matchup.

The switch is reportedly about "optics" and not any sort of disciplinary measure for the Packers-Lions crew.
